utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. May we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honour. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom, Mark Harmon and Bronagh McKenna for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much and for the Defence. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the proceedings. Mr. Perisic is represented today by Daniela Tasic, Tina Drolec, Milos Androvic, Gregor Guy-Smith, Novak Lukic, and two new interns and these are David Montano and Michelle Ternus-Nugent. And with your permission we would like them to be in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Good, Mr. Starcevic. Again I got to do the ritual. You are still bound by the declaration that you made yesterday to tell the truth whole truth and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Starcevic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, yesterday we ended with Prosecution Exhibit 2418, which was a 30th Personnel Centre recommendation to end professional military service of a man named Antic. I want to complete the story on Mr. Antic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So if I could have 65 ter 9439.06 on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, you see the document in front of you on the monitor? Could you --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Kindly look at that document and ...

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: First of all, okay. Identify this document. This is an order of the chief of personnel administration of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army, and it's dated 5th of February, 1996. And it is a document which ends the professional military service for Zoran Antic, on the basis that he was absent without leave for five consecutive days.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we go to the end of the document, each of the documents and see who signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you see a name at the bottom right-hand corner, Mr. Starcevic, and can you identify the person?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Chief of the administration, Major-General Dusan Zoric.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So he is a member of the VJ; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, yesterday in court, at page 80 of LiveNote, you said that the judgement of a VRS military disciplinary court could not serve as a basis for terminating service of a VJ officer. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who does have the ultimate authority, Mr. Starcevic, to discipline, to punish, and to terminate from service VJ -- a VJ soldier who was transferred to the VRS or transferred to the -- to serve in the SVK?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, if it is a member of the Army of Yugoslavia, then it is under the jurisdiction of a certain senior officer of the Army of Yugoslavia. Of course, you cannot exactly say which one because that depends on the order that is referred to in the introduction of the document. In any case, it would be in the hands of the authorised official of the Army of Yugoslavia, if that person happens to be a member of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And in this case, Mr. Starcevic, if we take a look at the document and the text of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we can go to the first page of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And under the statement of reasons, we can see that there is an reference in the second line to Mr. Antic being absent without leave from the 13th of March, 1995, which was the date which was referenced in the previous document, P2417, which was the judgement. So in terms of the termination of Mr. Antic, then, can you give us your view in respect of the procedures and the process that was used to terminate him, as reflected in this particular document that's before you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evidently in this case, Mr. Antic was terminated from service because he left a military unit without permission and spent longer than five days absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Five days absent from the VRS unit in which he was serving?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where he was serving --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this is a leading question that does not arise from this document. I don't know how Mr. Harmon can put this question to the witness who's now just providing his own expert opinion. Now we're in the again terrain of his expert opinions and not facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the previous two documents reflected the unit in which this witness was serving, so in terms of -- merely I'm putting what was contained in a previous document to this witness. I'm not leading him to that conclusion. I'm referring him back to the two previous documents that he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what I thought. I thought that was established yesterday. Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And so -- yeah, okay, the question has been answered, I see, on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could this be admitted into evidence and given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stand by the objection and would like to have this document just MFI'd, based on Article 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: May I comment, Your Honour, on Article 27?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Just ... Your Honour, there's -- let me just have one minute to look at this. I'll reserve my arguments for later, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. I thought we had agreed on that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll do that later on, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I then have this given an exhibit number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it please be given and exhibit number and marked for identification. Under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2419, marked for identification, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now, if I could, Mr. Starcevic, to three documents and solicit your views. They are in the same theme we had been pursuing in respect of Mr. Antic's documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could, first of all, have 65 ter 9440.03 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Sir, let's -- have you seen this document before coming into court today? This deals with a -- this is a military disciplinary court judgement relating to a number of persons, including Major Vujic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it, but I really don't know if --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. We'll go through this document and slowly. Let, first of all, if we go to the end of the document to determine which court this was. And we can do what we did yesterday, look at the last portion of the decision, and it says on the area of instruction on appeal. Can you tell the Court -- first of all, this is a military disciplinary court of which jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if we could go to the front page, then, of this document. We can see in this -- just the upper left-hand corner, we can see this is a military disciplinary court attached to the air force and PVO command. There is a number of this decision. It is 1-Dis 33/95 and dated 20th September, 1995. If we could go to the second page of the English. And we can see in the second page of the English the judgement of the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you see that? Do you see that in your language, Mr. Starcevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Identified in the judgement is Major Vujic and --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- it indicates that -- where it says there guilty, the first line -- again these people were serving in a unit VP 7272 in Banja Luka; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if we could see what the sentences were in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could go to page 3 in English. And ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you see what the sentence was for Mr. Vujic, number 2?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was the sentence?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Termination of service as an active member of the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this is a series of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have this document marked for -- given an exhibit number and marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it be given an exhibit number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2420, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Harmon, do you want to keep it under seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Under seal, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now could we take a look at a related document. It is 65 ter 9440.04. Mr. Starcevic, this is a document from the command of the RV and the air force and the anti-aircraft defence, and it's dated 29th of January, 1996. It is addressed to the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army to the personnel administration, and it refers to a document from the 30th Personnel Centre, and it gives a number. Now, have you seen this document before, Mr. Starcevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really cannot remember. It's possible that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- let me focus, first of all, on the first paragraph. It says: "In the attachment, we are sending you the judgements rendered by the military disciplinary court attached to the command of the air force and PVO of the 30th Personnel Centre with which the following members of the RV and PVO were sentenced to termination of service ..." Do you see first person --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The first person is Mr. Vujic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Vujic; yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vujic, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we go to page 2 of the English version. If we could scroll down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you see the section, Mr. Starcevic, that reads: "I am sending you the judgements because we have assessed the following ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In the English it's at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you focus, Mr. Starcevic, on the paragraph that is immediately below the words I just read. It starts with: "That the proceedings of the trial ..."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, I cannot read all of the text, all of the reasons because the copy is pretty illegible, the -- below the paragraphs that you referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me, if I could, assist you, Mr. Starcevic. I can read the text very slowly that I'd like to you comment on. It reads as follows: "I am sending you the judgements because I have assessed the following: That the proceedings of the trial and the rendering of the judgements were not conducted in accordance with the regulations on military discipline in the VJ. Namely, the persons involved are members of the RV and PVO who have been sent temporarily to work in the units of the 30th Personnel Centre; and therefore, in our opinion, the conducting of proceedings for the violation of military discipline by the above members of the RV and PVO is in the jurisdiction of the military disciplinary court attached to the command of the air force and PVO; ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. But I am confused by the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Tell me -- let -- before you comment on that, on the text, Mr. Starcevic, let me -- first of all, let's identify which document -- which entity has created this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we go to the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you identify who the person is who sent this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel General -- Lieutenant-General Ljubisa Velickovic, commander of the RV and the PVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know in which army he served in?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So if we can go back to the text that I have referred to. Could you then put -- assist us with this text in what your view is of this text?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Evidently here, General Velickovic believes that proceedings cannot be conducted against persons temporarily deployed to the 30th Personnel Centre before the military courts of that centre, and that possible proceedings would be under the jurisdiction of the disciplinary court at the command where he was, the command of the air force and the anti-aircraft defence of the Army of Yugoslavia. And if you're seeking my opinion, I believe that General Velickovic's position is well grounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, I would ask that this document be admitted and given an exhibit number and placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, will you help us please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2421, marked for identification, under seal. Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to comment on this document. I have no objection to this document being admitted, and I'm not seeking that it be MFI'd because the witness has personal knowledge of this particular matter relating to General Velickovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Then we're happy to have the MFI status removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Will you please remove the MFI status, Madam.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P2421, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, finally, Mr. Starcevic, to complete the story of Mr. Vujic, I would like to show you 65 ter 9440.05. Mr. Starcevic, please take a look at this document, and tell us if you've seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's hard to say if I've seen it or not. But I've seen a lot of these documents this one, also, I assume. But I really cannot be 100 percent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. This is a document that relates to the previous two documents. It related to Mr. Vujic, and it's an order terminating his service, and it's dated 12th of October, 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we see just at the end -- could we see at the end who is -- the name appears at the bottom. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you see the -- can you identify the person who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Major-General Vladan Marjanovic. I assume that he is the commander of the RV and the PVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So we can see that nine years after the -- the concern expressed by the previous general that Mr. Vujic was finally terminated from [indiscernible]?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is only for purposes of completing the story, Your Honour. I ask that this be admitted, marked for identification, and placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it please be given an exhibit number, marked for identification, and placed under seal, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2422, marked for identification, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if we could turn to another series of documents related to the same topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, I'm going to, first of all, to introduce these documents, I need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: First of all, if I can have 65 ter 9549 doc ID 06427102 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you still want to be in private session, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, this is a protected document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is merely to identify who is the person whose record I'm going to show on the next page, where there is no identification. So this is a -- can you identify what this is, Mr. Starcevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a personal sheet of Kosojevic, Ljubo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could this be marked for identification and given an exhibit number, marked for identification, and placed under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence, marked for identification, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2423, marked for identification, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 9549.01 as the next item on the monitor. Okay. By way of explanation, Your Honour, the reason I introduced the previous document because there is no identifiers on this document, but this is contained within the personnel file. So if we could --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could focus your attention, first of all, on two items, Mr. Starcevic, can you see the line that reads: "Commander of the battalion." It is in the fifth line.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell us in which unit Mr. Kosojevic was serving?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Light Infantry Brigade of the land forces of the 30th Personnel Centre in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if we go to the far right-hand column, it says PSU and then there are some numbers. Can you tell us what those mean?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was an order issued by the personnel administration, pursuant to which he was assigned to this post.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And, finally, let me direct your attention to the text at the bottom of this document. Can you tell us what that text means, what it is and what it means?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that his service is being terminated on account of a five days absence without leave, and, again, pursuant to a document issued by the personnel administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the number -- the identifying number on that document was 200-59, it was issued on 9 May 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could this be marked -- given an exhibit number and marked for identification and placed under seal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number, MFI, and u.s.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2424, marked for identification, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have -- yes. Could I have 65 ter 9549.06 on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, if you just review that document and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we can scroll down for the benefit --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, what is this document, Mr. Starcevic, that's before you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This actually implies initiation of procedure to terminate the professional service for Ljubo Kosojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And which entity made the proposal to terminate his service?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the seal, this was proposed by the Deputy Commander, Colonel Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we scroll the English so that we see what the witness is talking about, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. You have to go to the next page, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And there's a stamp on this document that we can see in the left-hand corner from the General Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we -- let me just make one other observation on --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On the statement of reasons in this document, Mr. Starcevic, we can see that Mr. Kosojevic had abandoned his units to which he had been assigned to perform his tasks on 24 November 1994. So that's the date he went AWOL. He went AWOL; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now the proposal as we see on this as well is -- references Law on the Army of Yugoslavia, Article 107, item 2, which we have discussed previously. So this --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this, as we see in the upper left-hand corner this document was issued by the Drina Corps command; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So this -- this document, then, Mr. Starcevic, is a proposal to the -- to terminate this gentleman, correct, based on Yugoslavia Army law?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me just -- this leads up to the final document, which I'd like to show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If this could be given an exhibit number, MFI'd, and under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that will be Exhibit P2425, marked for identification, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Finally, in this series, sir, let me go to 65 ter 9549.08. Could you take a look at that document, Mr. Starcevic, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's, first of all, let's identify it. It's an order. It's order that was referred to in the exhibit earlier, 200-59, and it's an order of the personnel administration of the Yugoslav Army, dated the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we go to the end of the document to see who is the person whose name appears at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Whose name is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of the personnel administration, Major-General Dusan Zoric.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in this case, this -- what does this document do in relation to the service of Mr. Kosojevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that his service in the Yugoslav Army has been terminated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And we earlier saw, Mr. Starcevic, a recommendation from the Drina Corps in the VRS to terminate Mr. Kosojevic's service. Can you comment for us on process under which Mr. Kosojevic was terminated. In other words, on the basis of a recommendation from a separate army, is it proper to terminate a soldier in the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult to perceive this matter in this way. The proposal -- or a proposal is not a binding document, although it is part of a formal procedure leading to termination. It is not customary to submit a proposal from one army to another. I think that this is not a legal issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say you think it's not a legal issue, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To put it simply, the proposal, per se, as a document, does not imply any obligation on anyone. The jurisdictions have been set up in a different manner, and the only thing that is legally formalised is to render a decision based on somebody's proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this be admitted, MFI'd, and placed under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it be given and exhibit number, MFI'd, and under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P2426, marked for identification, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I want to change the topic a bit, Mr. Starcevic, and look at one final exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could have Prosecution Exhibit 1009 on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Take a moment, Mr. Starcevic, just to look at this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are these documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- the same documents in different versions?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It should be a single version of one document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, what I mean is in different languages, two languages. The formatting doesn't look like -- correspond.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the next page of this document in B/C/S is the proper one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Okay. Now we've got something that looks like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we -- could you just take a look at this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And could we zoom in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now I think, actually -- actually, I think this is not the [indiscernible] English version of this document. The document -- maybe we could proceed this way. The document ID on this document that I'm looking for is 06465198. It's page 3 of the B/C/S and page 1 of the English. Yes, that appears to be what I'm looking for in the -- yes, we now have the proper documents on the monitor. Thank you. Mr. Starcevic, this is an order. Can you tell us whose order this is?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Scroll down a little on the -- or up a little on the B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order of the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this is an order on supplying the 30th and 40th Personnel Centre with weapons and military equipment ; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, the 30th and 40th -- assuming the 30th and 40th Personnel Centre is the VRS and the SVK, respectively, is this a proper order from President Lilic directing that the Yugoslav Army provide weapons to those separate armies?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to correct you. That's not an instruction; it's an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I said order, Mr. Starcevic. I did say instruction so perhaps there was translation --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard in the translation an instruction or a guideline.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it is an order.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] That means that this is a binding document to -- for the recipient. It is it difficult to say whether this is inappropriate or not, because this is based on a political decision. There is no obligation under the law for the Yugoslav Army or Yugoslavia, as a country, to provide supplies to any other army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. So if we take a look at the second paragraph of this document, it says: "The chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army is hereby authorised to reconcile the requests of the 30th and 40th Personnel Centre with the means of the Yugoslav Army and specifically regulate the method and procedures for providing the supplies from item 1 of this Order." Now, does this order, Mr. Starcevic, in your view, give General Perisic the authority and the right to distribute weapons, ammunition, other supplies to the VRS and to the SVK?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He's actually being ordered to take care about providing these supplies, but in doing so, to bear in mind the available resources of the Yugoslav Army. Therefore, he is authorised which means that he is obliged and authorised to supply the 30th and the 40th Personnel Centres but to take due care about their needs, on the one hand, and the availability of the resources of the Yugoslav Army to provide these supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Starcevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no additional question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I -- I'm fine, yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Starcevic. I'm going to ask you questions on behalf of the Defence team of Mr. Perisic. Two pieces of information before we start this cross-examination. The two of us speak the same language, and we understand each other more quickly than the interpreters will be able to translate. Therefore, I kindly ask you to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We're still in private session, Your Honour, so I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session. Thank you, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, I will kindly ask you to pause after my question, and I will do the same after you answer, so that the translation will reflect properly what we are saying. And, secondly, we have prepared documents that we're going to discuss which are in the database of this court, but I also have provided hard copies. I've notice that you have problems in reading the documents from the screen, so, therefore, if you encountered any problems in that sense, and you prefer hard copies with the leave of the Chamber, I will provide this for you. So feel free to ask for hard copies whenever you need it. I'm going to start with the first set of questions by establishes a context that we are -- context that we are going to discuss later and that is a historical and social context which is something that you have been testifying to in these previous few days, but we would like to paint a picture relating to the period with which you are personally acquainted. I assume, Mr. Starcevic, that you will agree with me that the single legal system that was in place in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was, in many respects, ceased to function in the last years of the existence of that state?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's definitely true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That primarily was reflected in the paralysis of the federal institutions?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, primarily for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that the political events and the conflicts that ensued while this country was still existing in the late 1980s actually brought about a total paralysis of the legal system in the country and, for the most part, in the functioning of the federal state.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me in saying that the political reality of disintegration of a legal system required new systems to be put in place that would reflect the changes in society?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes that would have been a reasonable way to pursue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You cannot change society in line with the regulations, but it should be vice versa. This is what I generally perceive as political changes.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, yes. This is generally applicable everywhere. Law, as a science, is a little bit lazy in following, reflecting social changes, and it's lagging behind which is only a logical consequence of the nature of the law as science.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So when a changes in a legal system need to be made, they are based on the previously adopted political decisions.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Because the law is also a result of a political struggle of various tendencies in society and it creates a political concept only until such time when it is adopted as the law. When that happens, it loses its political connotations and notions, and this is what today we define as the rule of law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The disintegration of the Socialist Republic of Yugoslavia was very much reflected and had a strong impact on the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With the withdrawal of the JNA from Slovenia, Croatia, Macedonia, and subsequently partly from Bosnia and Herzegovina actually led to the transfer of a large number of military personnel to what was later to be called the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true to a great extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In fact, the whole Military District dissolved very quickly that used to function before and had their zones of responsibility. So in actual fact, they ceased to exist; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that was the worse consequence because we don't only have the legal termination, but we also have the factual termination, because the basic principles and norms that you used to function suddenly ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you will agree with me that this has created huge problems for the authorities and the state and for the political leadership of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether that was a problem for the entire political leadership of Yugoslavia, I'm not quite sure about that, because I believe that part of what we consider to be the political leadership of Yugoslavia at the time were particularly those who contributed to the whole situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that the Chamber is fully aware of that. I may have not been quite precise. If we look at the situation in 1992, when was the time when the JNA left the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and after May, when the constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was established, I'm referring to this political leadership; and my question was whether they saw the problem, this political problems.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was particularly problematic for the remaining part of the country that was called the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, a huge number of professional officers of JNA were left without their posts per establishment, and they all arrived the FRY. On the other hand, let us shed a different light on this context which is important. Military conflict kept going on in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. We are talking about 1992, and we will come to the time when Mr. Perisic was appointed the Chief of Staff. In this military conflict that was raging in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, there was active participation of many professional servicemen of the then-JNA, both while it was still there and after its withdrawal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The speakers are kindly asked to slow down a bit and pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpreters would like you to please slow down. And before you even ask the next question, can I understand one thing. The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was established, and after it had been established, the army continued to be called the JNA or did it also -- did the change to the VJ at the time that it -- the country changed to the FRY?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we will come to that. But we can put this question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, we know that the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia was adopted later, but does the constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia create a new term and practically was the Army of Yugoslavia formed under the constitution that was adopted?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's -- it would be hard to say that it was formed. What was left of the former JNA with the adoption of the new constitution had its name changed, and it became the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When was the constitution adopted, approximately? All right. We're not going to -- all right. Later we will show the document. We will come to that and then we will ... I assume that you are familiar with the fact that these officers of the former JNA, because now I'm moving to the formation of the new armies. You will agree with me, first, that at a certain point in time the armies were formed -- I'm going to start an order, the Army of the Republic of Croatia, the Army of the Army of the B and H, the Army of Republika Srpska, the Serbian Army of the Krajina, and even there is an Army of Herceg-Bosna, but the Army of Macedonia. Would you agree with me with me that after the forming of those armies, the gist or their corps was formed by former JNA officers who had had joined those armies. What you are aware of from your personal experience, please?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many of those newly created armies had former JNA officers as their members who had opted to join them, based on an ethnic, territorial, or some other criterion and remained in these newly formed states. But it seems to me that it is a little bit unfortunate that even though they had opted for those armies, not all of those newly formed armies gave them a key role. In many of those armies, the key roles were assign to some other people who, overnight without any kind of military experience or education or knowledge, were promoted to the highest ranks, and although many -- well, many. A fair number of former members of the JNA had opted to remain in their new states. It is my impression that they, for the most part, were under-appreciated in those new countries and armies, although there are exceptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are also aware, probably, that certain JNA officers joined those armies and, in the course of 1992, after they returned to the territory of the FRY with the JNA, they later went back and voluntarily joined those armies? I'm talking about the period before the Personnel Centres were formed. We will come to that topic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with that, and some of those examples are honourable examples of those officers' contribution to taking their units out of the chaos, bringing them back to safety, and only then opting to return to the newly formed armies of these new states.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us look at one document now. It's document 1D04-0216. The document has three pages, and we will cover it quickly. This is a report on the numerical strength of personnel financed from the budget of the Yugoslav Army. The document is a document from the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army from August 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And please go ahead and look at the document. And then, after you finish, I can put a few questions to you. And if you don't see it very well on the screen, I can provide a hard copy. And when you read it, please, let me know.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document, can we scroll it up a little bit just so that we can see who signed it. The document was signed by chief of the General Staff of the army of -- the Yugoslav Army, Colonel General Zivota Panic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You aware that he was the chief of the General Staff of Yugoslav Army before Momcilo Perisic, and this is a document from that period immediately before the change at the top of the General Staff. Do you agree that this document indicated, particularly in relation to the first passage, that there is an certain number of people in the Yugoslav Army -- actually, in the army of Republika Srpska, who are financed by the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is something that does arise from that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 3, it's a larger paragraph, persons are mentioned who are temporarily engaged, according to Article 271 of the Law in the Service in the armed forces, which was in force then; this is what is meant; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So that was the basis on which they were, at the time, sent to the Army of Republika Srpska and the Army of the Serbian Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then it says here in the next sentence: "The status of these persons is regulated in the service of the Yugoslav Army, even though, in practice, they are not occupying these posts ..." This document indicates state of affairs whereby person who are not in the Yugoslav Army on certain duties are recognised, the rights that they would have; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For a moment, can we now look at page 3 of this document. This document is a table which speaks for itself, practically, and it indicates their, let me put it that way, status as officers, non-commissioned officers, contract soldiers, civilians, meaning all those four categories that we're going to see later that are appearing in the Personnel Centres and in those decisions, which will take place in 1993, which were present before -- actually, before General Perisic was appointed to the chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please -- I would like to tender this document for admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what's the relationship between the witness and this document compared to what we've been dealing with earlier?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that this witness very clearly and factually indicated here that he is aware of the facts from this document. That is the way I put the question. Well, let me -- I'm going to tell you now, Your Honours, although later there will be document where I'm going to agree for them to be admitted as MFI, if Mr. Harmon begins to present my position [as interpreted]. But I am putting witness -- to the witness questions that officers from the JNA, as a fact witness, left, and maintained a specific status in the service. So that is the sense in which I put questions to this witness, and I think that this is how I did establish the condition between the witness, his factual knowledge about matters that are written in the document, and the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you -- if you -- if a document says it's 7.00 and the sun has arisen, and I read it and I say, Yes, agree. It is 7.00. The sun has arisen, then does that establish the relationship between me and the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I am aware of that. I'm just trying to make sure we play the game; what is good for the goose must be good for the gander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your Honour, I still -- my problem of interpreting Article 27 of the guide-lines is perhaps too restrictive. Well, let's not go into it. We're going to write -- perhaps the best thing would be to put it in writing, but the way I am interpreting the guideline, Article 27, indicates that witness knows certain facts from the document, not for him to read them. That is how I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D113.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, can you please tell me, if you know, I'm going to ask you about the general status -- statutory rights of the member of the Yugoslav Army, or, rather, JNA. You are aware, on the basis of the laws that were in force at the time of the JNA, the Law on Service in the JNA and regulations that were in force at the time, and later with the adoption of the Law on the Yugoslav Army and regulation which accompanied this law, that each member of the JNA or Army of Yugoslavia had certain statutory rights arising from their professional position?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These rights also are due to them; in certain cases, to members of their families; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The right to years of -- pensionable years of service is a result of the years that a certain person spends in active service in the JNA or the Yugoslav Army; and, on that basis, they have the right to a pension from the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under certain regulations, this granted them the right to a family pension on the basis of their status in the Army of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And rights to social and health benefits and the rights, also, included the members of that person's family, arising from their service-related status; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that -- would you agree with me that in the JNA, in the Yugoslav Army, there was a well-known plan of health benefits which was very comprehensive and quite privileged, compared to regular health services?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to avoid the word "privileged" because that also affects me as a member of the armed services. We were not privileged. It's just that the level of that health of service was at a higher level because the people who provided it were better educated. They were more professional, better trained, and very dedicated to their job.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have this image from that time that those people who did not have service-related medical health rights that the members of the army had in a way regretted not being able to use the services of the military medical academy, which in Belgrade, in relation to other medical institutions had a reputation as a -- a pre-eminent professional high-quality service provider; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because of that, members of the army and the JNA also at their disposal the possibility to use resorts, hotels, recreation facilities, which were the exclusive property of the army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to remember everything. You also had the situation where, based on their status, members of the army had double years of service; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not all of them, just those who were performing services which, in a way, involved service under more difficult conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps we can go on a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. On that privileged note, we will take a break. Come back at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, Mr. Starcevic, wait a little bit after you start your answer. A while ago, we had a discussion concerning status-related rights deriving from the military status, and that is the housing rights relating to the service. Would you agree that under the Law on the Army, with regard to their length of service, exercise and enjoy certain rights in terms of housing and that is to be given an appropriate residence from the army; that is to say, from the state; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know that this category of being given a flat by the state, is somewhat incomprehensible in this Tribunal, which was deemed to be socially-owned property. What it meant is that certain person and his family were given a flat for use for an indefinite period of time without being given the right to ownership. This is in a nutshell; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is how it was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And after that, regulations were adopted that these flats could be bought at a non-market prices, that is to say, at lower prices, whereby they became owners of these flats and had full property rights on them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to all the status-related rights that I mentioned before, let me ask you this: If somebody ceases to be a member of the military will lose all these status-related rights granted to him under the law; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in principle. But depending on the length of service that he accumulated prior to the termination, he may retain some of the rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which rights in particular, the pensionable years of service, I presume?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me take you as an example. You left the Yugoslav Army at a certain point. Which particular rights have you retained that you enjoyed previously as a member of the military?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have exercised the right to a reduced pension, the right to the flat that had been given to me, the right to health insurance in military facilities, as you described them as privileged. I also retained the right of use of holiday resorts that belonged to the army as retired military serviceman, and there may be some more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, these right, as you said, you earned as a military pensioner; right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A theoretical question: If you went to live in another state, you wouldn't be able to exercise your right to the pension from the army. You would probably lose the flat used by you here, unless you had bought it beforehand; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The right to pension is suspended for as long as someone lives outside his homeland or state, and that includes also right to use the flat, if the flat is unused for a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, this relates to civil rights. There is a provision that the tenancy right can be stripped off someone if they are not using the flat.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That applies to the cases of persons who had not bought their flats.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now focus to another issue, which is also important, in my view, for the context that we're going to discuss. You will agree with me, and I think you already mentioned that when we talked a while ago about the departure and the return of JNA officers to and from Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, et cetera. Would you agree that there was a large number of JNA officers and later VJ officers who felt a moral obligation to help the people from which they originally hailed? I mean Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina in the first place. That is not in dispute, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was, first of all, a personnel question for all these officers, but I think that the majority of them felt a moral obligation to be in the region of their origin, particularly because they had families in those regions, parents, relatives, or maybe even property.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I suppose you will agree with me that for those who wanted to leave and did leave to join these armies, it was important for them that the status of their families who had stayed behind in the FRY be regulated, based on their acquired rights?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose that was of paramount importance for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at document P730. This is quite a long document, and I wouldn't like to go through the whole of it. Let us just look at the introductory part and then -- paragraph 1, and then we shall -- actually, I'm interested only in paragraph 1. Perhaps I should have asked for page 3 first in B/C/S so that we can see who issued this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So can you please look at paragraph 10 on this page.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go to page 2, paragraph 7; and that's, I think, page 4 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see that this is a decision taken by the president of the FRY, Zoran Lilic. And it is based on the conclusion of the president of the FRY, dated the 4th of May, 1992, as it is stated in the decision. And this decision relates to the status-related rights of members of the VJ, those who are engaged in the Serbian -- in the Army of the Serbian Krajina. This is an undated document, but you will agree with me that this document was signed by Mr. Zoran Lilic, president of the FRY, and that it was issued after the promulgation of the constitution of the FRY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the term "army" -- "Yugoslav Army" is being used here. Let me first ask: Have you ever seen this document in its entirety? Has Mr. Harmon or anyone from the Prosecution shown you this document before?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing it at that time, but some parts of this decision look familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Harmon would not object to my statement that the Personnel Centres are never mentioned in this document. Now, since are you familiar with the decision on the establishment of the Personnel Centres, and you spoke about that in examination-in-chief, does this fact stated in Article 7, which is that these military personnel shall retain their status in the Yugoslav Army and also enjoy all the rights deriving from that status pursuant to the applicable regulations? Is this portion of the document in correlation with what was going to be later put in, in the order of the Personnel Centre and the status in the service?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is very difficult to claim explicitly and establish explicitly, but it looks to me that this is the case, because through -- in paragraph 3 of Article 7, which stipulates the way in which the status -- service status of these personnel is going to be determined by a VJ officer in charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we scroll. Please let's see paragraph 3 of paragraph 7. Thank you. What happened now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's paragraph above Article 8, and this is the one that Mr. Starcevic commented upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see it above it. This is the first paragraph in the English version on this page, and this was what Mr. Starcevic commented on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From your personal experience while you worked in the Ministry of Defence and the Yugoslav Army, although the Ministry of Defence was independent of the army, but you were part of that system, were you aware that in 1992 and 1993 active-duty officers of the SVK and RSK were receiving salaries from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was aware of that in an unofficial fashion, because in my post, I was not involved in these procedures, and I didn't know much about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we don't need this document anymore. Therefore, it can be removed from our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order to wrap up this context, I'm going to address only one more topic with you. Would you agree with me, Mr. Starcevic, that in the close proximity of the FRY where it actually had its border, there was a severe and fierce civil war raging in 1992, all the way through the year in which the Dayton Accords were signed?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that that represented a permanent danger of the war spilling over into the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may draw some conclusions on that, but I can agree with you that that posed a danger to relations between Yugoslavia and the war-torn zones. And if I may add this, I think that up until official recognition of the new states, i.e., Croatia, Slovenia, and later Bosnia-Herzegovina that was, in essence, a civil war in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're referring to the recognition by the international community?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another question: Would you agree with me that this war that surrounded the FRY could have an effect to a potential hot beds of conflict? And I'm referring to Sandzak and Kosovo and that it had direct bearing on the security situation within the FRY itself?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have some, more or less, direct knowledge due to the duties that I continued to be involved in after leaving the army. I, myself, could see direct consequences, second-hand experience of the consequences of conflict in certain areas of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to these regions that I mentioned Sandzak and Kosovo? Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, mainly those areas and also some other areas of multi-ethnic composition of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I suppose that this problem arose because these multi-ethnic communities had some links with the ethnic communities in the war-torn areas outside of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you would agree with me in view of what we mentioned at the begin, when we spoke about social changes that accompanied the disintegration of the country, that all of this led to a need to create stability in the country by taking political decision and thereby pre-empt or prevent the outbreak of war in the territory of the FRY?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Although I don't consider myself to be an expert in politics, I believe that the need for that was quite obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just interrupt. Mr. Starcevic at page 41 line 11, when you say "outside of Yugoslavia," which country are you referring to? Sorry, it's not you. It's Mr. Lukic. It's part of the question, I'm sorry. What do you mean by Yugoslavia there, sir? I'm asking you. Are you asking -- that's the translation of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The context of my question was after the formation of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Perhaps I wasn't precise, but I was thinking of Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And I believe that Mr. Starcevic understood my question in that way. That is, from the May of 1992 onward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You meant the FRY. Thank you, that's what I wanted to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The context of my question, of course, I did mention the period of 1991, but, first of all, what I was interested because of what we're going to talk about that context when the break apart -- when the country broke apart, when the FRY was formed, and then when the army fell apart. Mr. Starcevic, now we're going to move to a totally different topic. Now we're going to talk about command and control. These are categories that are mentioned in the law, one of the draftees of which is you, yourself, so I assume that you are going to be able to provide us with both your professional and knowledge that stems from your experience? Would you agree with me that the terms "command and control," in essence, are terms that refer to the functioning of every army from every single unit, up to the term "of the army."

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do you agree with me, that these principles or more or less similar in all the armies of the world?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would, first of all, say similar. I wouldn't say that they were identical. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. I think that I perhaps used a superfluous word. Would you agree with me that the principles of command and control in the JNA and the VJ were the terms of unity of command and singleness of command?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The principle of singleness of command means that there is just one person in command, issuing assignments and to whom one is responsible for the implementation of the issued assignment.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, generally speaking, but I would be a bit more precise. Singleness of command means that each member of the army can have just one immediately superior officer. That does not mean that he does not have some other superiors who is actually the superior to his immediate superior. But the immediate superior to anyone can only be one single person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And this second superior person can be only part of the chain of command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Subordination means practically what I have already said, that the superior makes decisions, and they refer to the immediately subordinated person.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Subordination, in essence, implies the duty of the subordinated person to execute orders issued by the superior commander, and the superior commander's right to issue those orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that is something that is frequently then referred to as the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. I think now that we're going to talk about the Law of the Army, your baby, let's say. We're now going to deal with Article -- with Exhibit P197. We're going to look at Article 3. And while we're waiting for it -- well, the Trial Chamber is already familiar with this Article. It states command on the army is based on principles of singleness of command, in terms of use of -- of forces and means, unity of command, and the duty to execute decisions, commands, and orders of the superior commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now what follows is -- what you also commented with Mr. Harmon, is Article 4 and then Article 5, which practically defined this chain of command, which starts with the president of the Republic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then Article 10 - this is on page 3 and the same page on the B/C/S; page 3 in the English - I'm sorry. Page 3 in English and page 2 in the B/C/S. I'm now going to ask you to comment on paragraph -- or item 2 of Article 10. This is what we were talking about already, that the superior commander is the person who performs or executes the command over a military unit.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The person who has been assigned to command a specific unit by a specific document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Law on the Army specifies just the Supreme Commander as the Supreme Commander in chief, but everything else then is derived from that, pursuant to the law in separate documents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to look at another law. That this is the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this is Exhibit 191, B/C/S page 1; and P191, B/C/S 1 and English page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Article 4, I don't need to read it. You can just read it for yourself. Would you agree with me that these are practically identical definitions of the terms from the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska, adopted in -- on the 1st of June, 1992, as it says. So it's identical to the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia that we already looked at?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, these are practically identical formulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at Article 173 of this law. On B/C/S, this is page 17; and in the English, it's on page 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Article 173: "Command in the army shall be founded on principles of unified command regarding the use of forces and means, single authority, obligations to enforce decisions, command and orders issued by superior officers." Let me say again that is practically the same formulation as in the law that we already looked at, the Law of the Army of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now let's look at the next article. I'm not going to read the entire article, but just the first paragraph, where it says that: "The president of the Republic shall be the commander in chief of the army. The president of the Republic shall ... " And then it notes all his duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down a little bit and look at number 14, last paragraph, that is thus the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Underneath the number 14 -- I'm practically reading the last practically paragraph under number 14 where it says: "The president of the republic can delegate certain command duties to the commander of the Main Staff who shall be responsible to the president of the Republic for the said duties." And then the next paragraph, very briefly, just the first part: "The commander of the Main Staff implements the command of the army pursuant to the powers vested in him by the president of the Republic, pursuant to the law ..." So we already have new, different categories in some terms, in relation to the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia. In the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska, of the Supreme Commander of - that's right - the army, is the president of Republika Srpska although this is not stated here. But that is clearly something that arises from the constitution and also the institute of the Main Staff, and the commander of the Main Staff is referred to; and would you agree with me that this does not exist in the Army of the Republic of Yugoslavia as a category; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The Law on Army does not contain the term "the Main Staff," but it has the term "the General Staff."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These Articles that we looked at from the Law of the Army of Republika Srpska, would you agree with me that in this law, the army of Republika Srpska is sets up as a separate army with a separate chain of command, going from the Supreme Commander down, and the Supreme Commander is the president of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the only possible legal interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at, very briefly, the Law on the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and that is 65 ter 637 -- I think we already admitted this page before. I'm only interested in the first page -- or, rather, it's B/C/S, page 11; and English, page 4 of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you saying it is already admitted?
