utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just been informed that only Article 161 of this law has been admitted and not this one. We only admitted only that particular article from this law and not the entire law as opposed to the previous two laws that we looked at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what is the number 637 denote? Is that an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, 6367 is the 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And D85 was actually just one article of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down for the purposes of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are being asked to slow down for purposes of interpretation. And what article do you want us to look at now on this page?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Article 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, we're not going to read. I'm only going to ask you whether this Article, in its contents, similar to, let me put it that way, this first paragraph, is similar to the principles we saw in the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia and the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Supreme Defence Council is mentioned here which is a category similar to the name referred to in our law. When I say "our law," I mean our Law on the Army of Yugoslavia. But just for a minute, let's look at Article 10. This is it on B/C/S, page 12; and English, page 1D040324, because it was not translated before, so we translated it now. Article 10 ... I'm going to put the same question to you. The contents of Article 10 are, well let me not say identical, but very similar to those solutions referred to in the Law of the Army of Yugoslavia and the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please tender this for admission. This one page -- or, actually, practically these two pages, practically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm advised that Article 3 is part of Exhibit D85. Then we'll just add Article 10 to D85. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, are we limiting the admission just to Article 10? Mr. Lukic sought the admission of the page, and he only referred to Article 10, so my request would be that the Article referred to only be admitted and not the whole page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The whole page where Article 10 appears, and the page where Article 3 appears will be admitted. Thank you so much. And can they be given an exhibit number -- oh, well, D85, eh?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to make one more comparison between these three laws, but we have to go back. First of all, Mr. Starcevic, can you tell me - this is a term that I use, but I don't know if it is a professional term - what is protected or protective facility of the army?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you analyse that in the legal sense then, a protective facility is something that the army has been entrusted to protect, pursuant to the constitution and regulations arising from the constitution, which means the territorial integrity, the constitution order from violent changes, and other assets or values as laid down in the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to look at P197 again on the screen, page 1, both in the B/C/S and in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that what is written here in Article 1? Is that a protective facility or object of the Yugoslav Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In essence, yes, although the legal terminology is a little bit unusual "zasticeni objekat voske," the protective facility or object of the army, and this is the Law on the Army. Based on that, the army is duty-bound to guard these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Army of Yugoslavia defends, and then it says the order of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the territory, the independence, and the sovereignty of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now can we please look at Exhibit P191, page, B/C/S, 1; and English, 1. Unlike the Yugoslav Army, the army the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as it was called at the time when this law was adopted, defends the sovereignty, territory independence, and the constitutional order of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to clarify the record, if I can go back to an answer and a question -- the question that was asked by Mr. Lukic. I'm referring to page 50. The reference he refers to -- it's line 6: "Is that what is written here in Article 1? Is that a protected facility or an object of the Yugoslav Army of Yugoslavia?" I'm looking at my translation of Article 1, and I don't see the term "protected facility." So I have a question: I would request that Mr. Lukic clarify either the question or be more precise, because I don't see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. That's been running through my mind too and wondering -- I was looking for that protected facility, and I couldn't see it anywhere. And I'm not even quite sure that I understand the use of that phrase, "protective facility." For me, the way it is being interpreted, I would have said protected facility or, I don't know. But just give us the word protected facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I was using a term that should have better be translated as an object of protection. This is how I'm using this term, and I'm using it, to tell you the truth, although I know that it's not stipulated as such in the law. But, logically speaking, I'm using it because I am having in mind things that are being protected, and I would really like to have a definition that is precisely set in the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but the only thing is the way you have, sort of, used it. I got the impression that if we look at the exhibit on the screen, we will see words to that effect, and I just didn't see words to that effect. But -- and I think the phrase object of protection, or whatever you said a little earlier, describes it better than protective facility. For me, protected facility means something that protects, not something that is protected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. Yes, that's correct. That is why I had this problem and I caused problem for the interpreters because I was using it as such, and we shall strive to be more precise in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the Army of Republika Srpska defends or protects the territory, independence, and the constitutional order of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is the fundamental difference that exists between these two laws that refer to different armies that have jurisdictions in two different states and territories.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is that fundamental difference? I thought all these armies defends the territory, the sovereignty, and the independence of their areas ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For the difference, you mean the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This may seem as to oversimplifies, but I wanted to demonstrate that the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina defended another territory, not the one that was defended by the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now let's look at Article 1.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat his last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Counsel, you are requested to repeat your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was misinterpreted. I wanted to demonstrate through these question that the armies mentioned in these laws protect the respective territories of their states.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but we know that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, very briefly, Article 1 of the Law on the Army of Serbian of Krajina stipulates that this army protects the territory of the Serbian Republic of Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, but I don't see this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is D85. I'm going to read it out to you in order to save time. Article 1 of the Law on the SVK reads: "The Army of the Serbian Republic of Krajina, hereinafter army is the armed force ... that defends sovereignty, territory, and independence of the Republic of Serbian Krajina." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, we have seen certain stipulations enshrined in three different laws relating to command and control, the chain of command, and the jurisdictions, i.e., the territories over which these armies have. Can we, therefore, conclude, based on these laws, that we are dealing with three completely separate armies?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If an officer is a member of a certain army, under the law, he is in the service of that particular army.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us draw another parallel that I see as important, and that has to do with transient provision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P191; B/C/S page 38, and English page 56. That's article -- I'm sorry. Yes, 191 is fine. The Law on the Army of Republika Srpska, Article 377, which reads: "Active duty officers, junior officers, and army personnel of the Yugoslav People's Army, citizens of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as those citizens of other states of the former Social Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, to wish to serve in the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and there is need for their engagement." Can we please look at the next page in English for the Judges to be able to follow what I'm reading. If we can scroll up the version in B/C/S, was adopted on the 1st of July -- 1st of June, 1992. In Article 308 it says that it came into force on the date of its publication. Now, can you comment on this article.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in what way you would like me to comment on it. This is, quite simply said, that all professional servicemen from the former JNA, on the date of this of this law coming into force, shall be reassigned to professional servicemen of the Army of Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't need to read it.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- provided they are either the citizens or -- they wish to serve in the Army of Republika Srpska and, of course, if there is an need for them to be engaged in the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that particular time, did they become members of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By the very act of being reassigned, they became members of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, coming to the Law on Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. That's P ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, 6367, 65 ter, 43 page in English, 43 in B/C/S, actually; and it's document 1D04-024, Article 320 of the law -- I'm going repeat. It's 1D04-0324 in English, and the B/C/S we can already see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This law was adopted, if we look at the top, on the 22nd April 1993. Without reading the Article, on the date of the adoption of this law, had the former members of the JNA become members of the Army of the Serbian Republic of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I move for this document to be admitted into evidence, only this page with Article 320 of the Law on the Army of the Serbian Republic of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's on the same page as Article 10, sir, which is already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But 320, in B/C/S, which carries the number 6367, that's page 65. This page wasn't admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. It's admitted -- Sorry, Mr. Harmon you were going to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Article 320 will be added to already existing D85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, finally, let us look at article -- actually, Exhibit 197, P197, that's the Law on the Yugoslav Army; Article 346, page 90 in English and page 31 in the B/C/S. Article 346. As far as I remember last time when you testified, we had some debate about the date of this law coming into effect. But without going into dates, there was a preliminary version and the official version of the 27th May 1994. This Article, 346, indicates that before the date of this law coming -- that on the day of this law becoming effective, the former members of the JNA become members of the army of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly ask the counsel to slow down. We cannot catch everything that he is saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you are being requested to kindly slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A couple of questions relating to the topic discussed with you with Mr. Harmon and on the rules and regulations that you discuss but from the point of view of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Due to my mistake and due to the speed, your answer was not recorded, Mr. Starcevic. Can you repeat, do you agree with me that on the basis of what is stated in Article 346, of the Law on Yugoslav Army, on the day of its coming into effect the former members of the Yugoslav People's Army became members of the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at exhibit - just bear with me for a moment - the Law on Defence; I think that's Exhibit P1183, page 4 in the B/C/S, and page 5 in the English version. Perhaps we can look at the following page in English first. It begins on this page, talking about 41 on the Supreme Defence Council. Article 41. And it states in paragraph 1 that the Supreme Defence Council adopts the plan for the defence of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what the defence -- what the plan for the defence of the country is.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a document laying out measures and procedures that should be carried out by all subjects of the National Defence, and pursuant to which they should prepare for the eventual defence of the country. I would like to emphasise this, "all subjects," because the Army of Yugoslavia is just one of the subjects of defence, and there is an crucial difference in this law compared to the Law on the Army, because this law regulates the rights, duties, and the relationships among all the subjects. It regulate a field of activity, while the Law on the Army regulates the institution of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't simply want now to just read this article because it speaks for itself. But can you please give you a comment of Article 4 [as interpreted], which the VSO establishes the needs in weaponry to carry out the defence?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see it to be able to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, you have it in front of you, so it -- of you, so it would be paragraph 1 of Article 4 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a very simply provision, stating that the Supreme Defence Council adopts a decision of what is required in order to defend the country, in terms of equipment and weaponry. It has the final decision on what is necessary to obtain, in terms of equipment and weaponry, in order to implement the plan that it has adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's go to the previous article, where it says that the president of the republic as the commander -- as the Supreme Commander of the Army of Yugoslavia practically -- if he realizes the decisions of the Supreme Defence Council through his orders, which he passes down or issues to his subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In essence, that's how it is because this law does not recognise the institution of the Supreme Commander, the president of the Republic, thus, implements the decisions of the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now, a little lower, to the federal government. This is it Article 52 [as interpreted]. We see -- this is Article 42, the authorities of the federal government, so what I'm interested in now is paragraphs 5 and 6. It refers also -- or they also refer to the national defence plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is the federal government the body that -- well, let me ask it like this: Is the federal government the one that holds the property rights of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In principle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said "titula," and perhaps I am making a problem for the interpreters with my words, the person who under the law is authorised to dispose with the property of the Republic of Yugoslavia is the government of the Republic of Yugoslavia. They are the title holder and have the right to transfer those rights to somebody else. They are the ones who are holding the title and entrusted with the assets, property of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that counsel is dealing with very complex things, and he is speaking very fast and not giving us enough time to process what is he saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the interpreters are really complaining now. They say you are very fast and dealing with very complicated matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, really, to the interpreters. I'm going to be slower and more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For a moment, can we put -- just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The military industry is in whose jurisdiction; do you know that? Or let me say the special purpose industry for the manufacture of weapons and military equipment.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance to what we were saying, it is under the jurisdiction of the federal government and within the federal government, if I remember correctly, it was under the authority of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like us to put on the screen now document 65 ter 7905. This is the Law on Property. I need page -- B/C/S, 6 and page 13 in English; Article 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This article states: "Movable items for special purposes are weapons, military equipment, and other movable items from Article 35, and Article 38 of this law, used by the federal ministry in charge of defence and the Yugoslav Army, as well as by the federal ministry in charge of internal affairs, for the defence and security purposes." And then the next Article: "The federal minister in charge of" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's note: We don't have this article on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Article 39. We lost it for a moment. Well, the previous page in the B/C/S is here, but the English we have lost. Article 39, can we please have both versions on the screen. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "The federal minister in charge of defence and/or federal minister in charge of internal affairs manage the procurement and use of movable items for special purposes from paragraph 1 of this article, under conditions stipulated by this law." This is what, let me put it this way, you already answered to me in advance, but it means that movable items which are defined in the previous -- actually in this article, paragraph 1, used by the Army of Yugoslavia about the procurement and disposal of these matters, meaning equipment and weapons, is something that the decision about -- is made by the federal minister of defence; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like us to tender this page of this law into evidence. This is the Law on Property, which is on the 65 ter list of the Prosecution. And we would like to tender this particular page into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Article 39 of 65 ter 07905 will be Exhibit D114.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Is that a convenient moment? We will take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I continue, just a slight intervention to the transcript, which evidently was a result of my speed. It's page 58, line 13, I referred to Article 41 of the Law on Defence, and what is written is Article 4. It should state Article 41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 58, line?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It should be Article ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now put back on the screen, P1183, the Law on Defence, of the FRY. B/C/S page 4 and English page 6. We're going to put a couple of questions only about what the Defence -- the Law on Defence says about the defence ministry, 43.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This Article deals with the authority of the federal Ministry of Defence in the defence system. What I'm interested in is paragraph 5, where it says that the federal defence ministry is authorised for equipping and arming to meet the requirements of the national defence. You worked at the defence ministry. Were there any separate parts of the defence ministry that were charged with the activities stipulated in this provision?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a sector in the defence ministry to deal with these tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And also, paragraph 10 of Article 1, it says that the federal defence ministry is organized for organising and preparing facilities for the production of weapons and military equipment and securing priority production for the needs of the Army of Yugoslavia. Is what is stated in this article something that indicates that there was special parts of the defence ministry that were in charge of these activities?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the same sector that I referred to before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please comment on Article 44?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same page in the B/C/S, and in the English version, it's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a different duty of the federal Ministry of Defence, and it's independent of what is stated in Article 43. I'm not going to read the whole article, but this is what I'm interested in: What do these inspection tasks consist of in terms of implementing decisions enacted by the president of the Republic of the Supreme Defence Council and the federal government --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, slow down, slow down, slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 2 of this article provides for the federal Ministry of Defence to perform inspections or checks of the implementation of the federal law -- the federal regulation, plans, and measures of the president of the Republic, the Supreme Defence Council and the federal government. Can you please tell us who did this within the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, there was a separate inspection and the gist of their activities, was, among other things, to oversee and monitor the implementation of decisions and documents adopted by the president of the Republic, the Supreme Defence Council, the federal government that referred to the defence of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This inspection was part of the Ministry of Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon asked you -- and now we're going to move to questions about the Personnel Centres. Before that, you said that you were not participating in any activities that had to do with the decisions to set up the Personnel Centres; is that correct? I assume that you were aware that the VSO meetings regularly were attended by the defence minister of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the chief of the General Staff. They were not members but they did attend these sessions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know, yes, they did attend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is the VSO? Is that the SDC?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, VSO, [B/C/S spoken], Supreme Defence Council, we use the abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall if you personally were present at the collegiums of the defence minister in line with your post -- you were just informed about the proceeds of those meetings?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I seldom attended, only when there was a legal issue on the agenda which was within the jurisdiction of the administration which I headed; and, of course, from the time when I became the head thereof, it was a customary practice for my superior, the chief of the sector within which the legal administration was, to attend. And, of course, he informed me about some of the tasks -- of the tasks and duties that were within the purview of my administration, but nothing beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the defence minister, within his scope of rights and responsibilities, informed his staff, his subordinate staff in the, ministry, about the information about that were passed on at the SDC meetings?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only surmise that he did. He would sometimes call me to come either alone or with my superior, my supervisor, but that mainly had to do with legislature that was being affected by my administration or if it had to do with some other legal issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please. Mr. Starcevic, that answer, starting at paragraph 10, I beg your pardon. Line 10, page 65, you say that you seldom attended: "Only when there was a legal issue on the agenda which was within the jurisdiction of that administration which I headed; and, of course, from the time when I became the head thereof. It was a customary practice for me, superior, the chief of the sector within which the legal administration was to attend. And, of course, he informed me ..." I'm a little confused. I thought he is you, because you are now the chief of the legal administration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This requires some explanation. I'm not sure I didn't follow the translation, and I didn't grasp what the problem was. There was a sector within the Ministry of Defence which was called, if I remember correctly, the sector for legal and personnel affairs. The chief, or the sector -- sector was there, and the sector had two administrations. My administration, which was the legal administration, and the other one which was the administration for personnel issue, let's say. Therefore, he was not part of any -- of either of these two administrations. The administration was part of his sector. What I wanted to say was that I think that the head of this sector regularly attended the collegium meetings because he was a member of the collegium. By virtue of my position, I was not a member of the collegium, but he did sometimes invite me, either at his own initiate or at the request of the minister to come and attend a meeting whenever legal issues were to be discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So your position was head of legal issues?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And he was head of legal issues and personnel, legal and personnel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You were under him [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, did you ever attend a meeting of the Supreme Defence Council, because, as we know, ministers were sometimes in the habit of bring some of their aides or associates with them. So did you ever attend a SDC meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only once, and quite intentionally and not by accident. That took place when the final draft was being prepared of the Law on the Army. It was being debated at the meeting of the Supreme Defence Council as well. And I went there in order to assist them to understand the provisions of the law from the legal point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at P229, which is the constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, page 46 in the B/C/S, and 44 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you could just briefly comment or as an introduction of what we're going to deal with, is article --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel please repeat the number of the article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the number of the article. The interpreters didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's Article 135, which reads ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, the command of the army under the constitution is within the scope of responsibilities of the president of the Republic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With respect to him, what was the role of the Supreme Defence Council? Are they in command or do they take political decisions that he, as the commander-in-chief, should implement?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me to make an observation, the way I read Article 135 is in rather different language. I think that you have quoted the formulation that I am familiar with. However, in paragraph 1, there is something that I'm not sure about but is quite different from that; namely, in Article 135, which I see in front of me, I read that in wartime and piece-time, the Army of Yugoslavia shall be under the command of the president of the Republic, pursuant to decisions of the Supreme Defence Council. I also remember text which says, in accordance with the decision -- decision taken by the Supreme Defence Council, I think that this difference is pretty serious, because, according to this language here, this would imply that the president of the Republic can exercise command only if he receives a prior decision from the Supreme Defence Council; whereas, in the text that I still remember, and I don't know if you have it with you, it reads that this is to be done in accordance with the decisions which gives him more freedom, which means that he does not necessarily have to wait for a decision by the Supreme Defence Council and doesn't seek one for each act of command, but, rather, conducts command in accordance with the already existing decisions. That is what I wanted to point out, and I'm really interested to know which of the texts is the genuine one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order to avoid any misunderstanding, and I think that similar problem occurred in another case before this Tribunal relating to different interpretations of one and the same article. I think that was in the Milutinovic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we can just put on the ELMO the text that you have just quoted for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, can I just add to the confusion. That same Article, 135, the second paragraph says the Supreme Defence Council shall be made up of the president of the Republic and the presidents of the member republics. The first Republic, with a capital letter, are we to understand that is the president of the Federation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that means the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You wish they had put the federal republic because when you just said republic and republics, it just doesn't make good sense to somebody who doesn't know the structure of the country. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a very usual expression in our language because the second part of the sentence is in plural. Therefore, these republics are then written with a lower case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can see the -- that difference, but, still ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have on the ELMO what we have just heard. Actually, what I read.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Starcevic, Article 135, I'm going to read it once again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just sorry to interrupt you -- oh, beg your pardon. Now we are seeing pictures. Okay. Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please scroll down a bit so that we can see what is written on top of this document. [In English] Down, down. [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Starcevic, can you tell us where does this document come from?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was published in the official military gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, you were an editor of the military official gazette for a period of time. Is that an official publication that promulgates such kind of documents to the public?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this case. The only official document that contains the constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia is the Official Gazette of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, whereas the official military gazette is an official documents that contains enactments passed by the Ministry of Defence or in some instances the General Staff and other bodies. However, the standard practice was that the military gazette republished some of the enactments, including the constitution. The same form as it was published in the federal -- in the gazette of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, can we look at Article 135 and can you please read out aloud slowly the first paragraph of this article.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In wartime and peacetime, the Yugoslav Army shall be under the command of the President of the Republic, in accordance with the decisions of the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I heard no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Apologies. Microphone was switched off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we get the interpretation then?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to repeat the answer -- the question. What you have just read is in accordance and consistent with what you remember was an official interpretation of paragraph 1 of Article 135 of what they call FRY constitution?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this to be an official text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not going to go into more details about what you mentioned about the distinction between what we read before and what we see on the screen now. But would you agree with me that the Supreme Defence Council was a political body that took decisions on the basis of which the president of the Republic, as the commander-in-chief of the Yugoslav Army, takes his own decisions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can I just seek clarification of one point. And that is: The text that is on the monitor, Article 135, in English it says pursuant to decisions, I can't read the Cyrillic and I don't know if that Cyrillic text also has pursuant or whether it has in accordance with the decisions of the SDC. So I want to make sure that the Cyrillic text in front of us and as part of an exhibit is correct and then we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's actually what Mr. Lukic has been trying to correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Right. But the source of this document, that is P229, is different than the source of the document that Mr. Lukic put on the monitor. As I understand it, the source of the document that Mr. Lukic put on the monitor was from the military gazette. The source of this document comes from a different source. So I just want it make sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But do remember that there -- what you saw from the military gazette is an English translation. You didn't see the -- what you call it? The B/C/S version. And I thought this is the B/C/S version of that which said pursuant to. And somebody who interpreted it made the mistake, interpreted in accordance with to be pursuant to. Now because Mr. Starcevic -- that's what I understand -- that's how I understand the process.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's why there is some confusion here. I want to make sure that the B/C/S document that is P229 in the record, in fact, has the correct words that Mr. Starcevic has corrected. We can correct the English. I don't want it to be a situation where the Cyrillic text has pursuant to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No. I heard the interpretation of what Mr. Starcevic to be saying, to be in accordance with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No. I agree with that. But he also related that in accordance to a different sourced document which was from the military gazette and not from the source of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Starcevic, can you come to the rescue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's very difficult. The only rescue from the situation is to ensure that we can see the Official Gazette of the FRY, because that would be the authentic source. But I do believe that the military gazette reprinted this official text, and I don't see the source here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But this is the military gazette, is it? Right. And you have just read it. It says in accordance with. So for me, it looks like the problem just arose when the -- this was translated. Are you with us, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. My only question is this, and I want just to clarify this: The text in the Cyrillic, in Article 135, the first paragraph does it use the word pursuant or does it use the word in accordance with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you are not with us. He's just repeated almost a third time. Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So the mistake arose when this document was translated into English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let's hear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that that version that comes from the military gazette is different from the version that we have in e-court, that was shown previously in Cyrillic. I'm not talking about the English version; I'm just talking about the Cyrillic. We have two different versions in Cyrillic. And according to Mr. Starcevic, the right version is the one that comes from the military gazette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Unfortunately -- yeah, I was talking from a person who is ignorant of the other language. Thank you very much, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks to Judge Picard, yes, indeed, it looks like even the two Cyrillic versions are different.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to be of assistance. The document that we had as evidence, P229, and which was on e-court, as far I can see, that document is a textbook. In B/C/S, that's a different document. What we were looking at now, as Mr. Starcevic explained, is the official military gazette, and there are significant differences between the Serbian Cyrillic text in the source that was in the e-court, which is P229, and what we have just shown on the ELMO. I'm going to propose, and I think that is the way the matter might be resolved in the best way is to actually obtain the FRY Official Gazette, and we can place it on the ELMO and then we can clarify this matter that has to do with the translations. If would you like to look at page 229 in the e-court, you're going to see that it is some sort of publication. It's not an official document of the Official Gazette. If you look at it on the e-court, you will see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: He see, that's the source of my concern, because this may not be the right text that's before Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think -- yeah. In fact, I think we must get this text out the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think we -- I agree with Mr. Lukic's suggestion. If all the parties in the court want the right text before us, I have no problem, we could reach a stipulation and substitute the right text for this particular article with a different text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. You may now proceed, Mr. Lukic, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if there is no need for this whole document to be tendered into evidence, but only after we obtain the Official Gazette of the FRY or because of the transcript, perhaps you would wish to have this entered into the court case. I have no objection to this document being tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: P229 is already in evidence. And that is what we saw on the ELMO, and it is correct. So it can stay there, and you can bring the FRY document just to confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What seems to be an anathema is this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. We're going to try to clarify this outside of the courtroom and to make an adequate evidentiary solution that will be then put forward by both sides. Let us now go back to that question regardless of the discrepancy in the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Supreme Defence Council, pursuant to the constitution, is the supreme political body which reaches its decisions, pursuant to which the president of the Republic exercises command over the army. I could define it that way too.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In some aspect, yes. The Supreme Defence Council is also a political body. However, in relation to commanding the army, there are no obstacles for the Supreme Defence Council to reach decisions, which would imply command, and then for the president of the Republic to be the one who would implement it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic, we have just spent some time correcting pursuant and replacing with in accordance. Your question now still uses pursuant. Can you -- can you try to stick to the letter of the -- of the law in Yugoslavia? That question from line 22 you said: "In some aspects, yes, the Supreme Defence Council is also a political" -- sorry, it is moving away. "The Supreme Defence Council, pursuant to the constitution which" --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I just wanted to deal on what I was focussing with.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But, anyway, it had to do with political decisions, and you said yourself what you believe and in which context was something a political decision and in which part. They referred to the part of the decision that refers to the command, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Like this now, I would ask now -- or ask to look at P733, please, which Mr. Harmon already called up. This document is a document that you've already looked at; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in your answers to Mr. Harmon, on page 54 and 48, line 8 of your testimony, you said that this document, this -- this order was adopted on the basis of the Law on the Army, Article 5. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The date of this document is the 15th of November, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it states here that the grounds for this order is the order of the president of the FRY, number 1/2-02-033/93, dated the 10th of November, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at document P731 on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us look at page 2 so that we can see who adopted this decision. Mr. Starcevic, who signed this order or command?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Mr. Zoran Lilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to the previous page now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Harmon or anyone else from the Prosecutor's office show you this decision during the proofing in preparation for your testimony? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not absolutely sure, but I think that I did see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: By the number and date of the decision, this would then be the basis for the order from Mr. Perisic that we saw earlier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you cannot really see that all that clearly from this document because it does not refer to the number of that order. But it does refer to the decision of the Supreme Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we didn't understand each other. The previous decision, the order on the establishment of Personnel Centres, we read it earlier, from the 15th of November, 1993, then we read that it refers back to the command of the president of the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thus, this decision, under this number, is dated the 10th of November, 1993, is the basis for the order on the establishment of the Personnel Centres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, let us look at the basis for this decision, and we can see that in the preamble. And it states that this decision by the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was adopted, pursuant to Article 135 of the constitution, and Article 4 of the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia, pursuant -- in accordance -- in accordance with the decision of the Supreme Defence Council. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't see a reference to Article 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that in the English version we need to scroll it up. I can see that there's a problem in the English translation, Your Honour, and you remarked it well that there is a part that was dropped or it's missing, so I think that we're going to have a problem that we will have to resolve by reading now what it says in the Serbian for the Trial Chamber. And because of the importance of this decision, we're going ask for an official new translation to be done. In the preamble it says, of the B/C/S version: "Pursuant to Article 135 of the constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Official Gazette of the FRY number 1/92 and Article 4 of the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia, Official Gazette of the FRY, (number 67/93) in accordance with the decision of the Supreme Defence Council, I hereby order ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Hmm. Even that -- reference to that number 1/92 is not there in the English. Just something wrong with the translation here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you, Your Honour. If we can continue with this document, and then we can ask for a -- an official translation, then later, to be -- for this new translation replace this existing translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. This is supposed to be Exhibit P731. Madam Registrar, can you give it a MFI status, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the status will be changed to marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Article 4 of the Law on the Yugoslav Army deals with the competence or authority of the president of the Republic in his capacity as supreme commander. And in paragraph 1, it says that the president of the Republic sets the foundations of the internal organisation, developments and equipping of the Yugoslav Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that that can be the basis for Article 4 of the Army of Yugoslavia to which the preamble of this decision refers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. That is the grounds, the granting of authority to the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the first paragraph of item 1. Please read it to yourself, this order. This first paragraph of Article 1 of this decision talks about persons who are subject to this decision to whom this decision applies, and these are two categories: Persons from the former JNA who remained in the territories of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina, and those who were received or admitted to Military Academies or to the military service of the JNA from those areas; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 2 in the B/C/S, and that would be practically page 1, paragraph 2, item 2, in the English version, where it says during that whole time, these persons entirely keep the -- retain all the rights pertaining to their rank and qualification and retain the salary they had in the post they occupied before the current assignment or they shall receive the salary provided for the new post, whichever is more favourable for the individual. These are service-related rights granted to these persons which arise from their status and rank that they had in the JNA or the Army of Yugoslavia before they went there, to these other armies; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That is the correct interpretation of this provision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, the next paragraph, 4, is a little bit longer, but it speaks about the tasks which are entrusted to the chief of the General Staff. I'm not going to read everything, but the last part of this paragraph states that the chief of the General Staff will determine the manner - I'm reading the last line from the bottom - procedure, and period to resolve the situation in the service and the protection of the rights arising from the service of these persons and members of their family.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Because it seems to me that, actually, here the -- in the command, a large part of what should be regulated is actually already regulated. In the previous text, in Article 4, it contains a lot of issues that actually represent the way in which these matters have been resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next paragraph speaks about the way in the way the chief of the General Staff can authorise other superior officer in the army. And then the paragraph after that, 5, is something that I am seeking your comment on: For the implementation of all the assignments from this order that fall within the competence of the federal Ministry of Defence ensure full coordination and cooperation between the General Staff of the army -- of the Yugoslav Army and this ministry. The article probably speaks for itself, but in view of what we talked about before, about the authorities of the defence of the -- ministry, defence ministry, some of the statutory rights are regulated by the Ministry of Defence, salaries, and so on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In essence, this points to the fact that the president of the Republic cannot issue commands to the ministry but does command to the chief of the General Staff to ensure this coordination with the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now that we've seen this decision, I'm going to put the following question to you: Would you agree with me that the decision on the establishment of the Personnel Centres was made by the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, in accordance with the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter did not hear the last part of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In accordance with what, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In accordance with the decision of the Supreme Defence Council; I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just make sure you finish your questions, okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at document P734?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now you're going to see your testimony during the examination-in-chief to Mr. Harmon [as interpreted], and this is the instruction on the manner of functioning and the programme of activities of special Personnel Centres. This document was shown to you before in these proceedings and we're just going to comment on a couple of excerpts and specifically that is the preamble of this instruction. In your view, what are the grounds of these instructions dated the 8th of December, 1993? On the basis of which did General Perisic draft this instruction?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can quote what is stated here, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. We won't. Is this previous order of President Lilic that we just spoke about now something that can be one of the grounds on the basis of which this instruction was issued?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly the number, which is N 1, then that is this order and it constitutes one of the basis for this instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at English page 2. It's a long document, but we're going to focus only on some parts of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Item 4 reads: "For people in the KC service of professional soldiers and civilians from entering into professional military service, the resolving of service status, promotion, exercising other service rights, and until cessation of professional military service, shall be regulated in line with the procedure and pursuant to the regulations relating to the Yugoslav Army." This is what this item reads. Is my understanding of this part in accordance with what we read before, and to which President Lilic's order refers to, about the setting up of the Personnel Centre says that their status-related rights would be regulated in accordance with the rules and regulations that apply to the Yugoslav Army? I'm talking about the status in the service. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only the status in the service but also other rights that stem from that stated in the same manner as it applied to other members of the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The focus and the emphasise here is on the rights that derive from the status.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This item particularly refers to their rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From your answers given in examination-in-chief, we have heard that the Law on the Army precisely and accurately regulates the status in the service. These rules and regulations were very simple and clear; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You would agree with me that there was no need to regulate something with a special order of the president of Yugoslavia, relating to something that is already stipulated by the Law on the Army concerning the status?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only that it is unnecessary, and it is also impermissible, because the Law on the Army is also binding on the president of the Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One of the answers about the reasons was that the underlying motive was because of those people were, at the time, members of different armies, because had they been members of the Yugoslav Army, they would exercise these rights according to the Law on the Yugoslav Army because all these status-related issues were covered by this law.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that is the crux of the problem. Who are you to consider a member of the army? And which army? In fact, whether a decision on that matter, who is a member of the army, should be taken on the basis of the legal status, or on the basis of some factual situations and status. It is difficult to choose between the two, but it seems to me that the overruling option should be the legal status because there are numerous factual situations, and they simply evade the possibility for them to be regulated according to the law and rules and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. You didn't answer my question though. Let me go back and be more precise, although your answer did cover a lot of the topic. Was there any reason to issue a special order by the president of the Republic, and consequently by his subordinate within the chain of command that refer to the individuals who were, according to their service status, members of the VJ, if that was already regulated by the law?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously there were no legal grounds for that, or wouldn't exist if we were to apply the interpretation that you have just provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now look at article -- excuse me, just one minute. Chapter 5, Article 33, page 7 in English, page 10 in the B/C/S. Item 33.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This chapter speaks about the return assignment and transfer of professional soldiers and civilian personnel from the Personnel Centre and Items 33 reads: "In keeping with service requirements, professional soldiers and civilian personnel sent or transferred to the KC" -- which stands for the Personnel Centre, "may be returned, assigned, or transferred to Yugoslav Army units/institutions with the consent or on the recommendation of the KC Main Staff." Main Staff of the Personnel Centre. If this paragraph stipulates that they can return to the Yugoslav Army, am I right in understanding it, that at this point of time, they were not in the VJ, since this paragraph provides for their return?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To put it simply, there is no other reasonable or legal understanding of this item. But if you view this paragraph separate from everything else that we have seen ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next paragraph of this same item speaks about the procedure. I'm going to skip this and move to paragraph 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm not sure the answer, the complete answer, of Mr. Starcevic was recorded. I refer to line -- page 87, line 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Hmm. It doesn't look complete, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is exactly what Mr. Starcevic said. But perhaps --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if I can be of any assistance, this was my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But it doesn't sound like a complete answer. You say, but if you view this paragraph separate from everything else that we have seen ... That's what it says there. What will happen if I view it that way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me try and explain. The counsel has offered an interpretation for which I said that there could be no other reasonable or legal understanding of this item. But, if we perceive this item separate from other provisions that we have seen before, but only if we perceive this item separate. This is another linguistic problem because this is not inconsistent with the English word order and syntax.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it -- the "but" was a new sentence. If it had been in one sentence, yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's precisely the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Starcevic, let's look at paragraph 34 and comment on it: "With the consent and on the recommendation of the KC Main Staff, professional soldiers and civilian personnel in the KC records whose professional military service ceases on many legal grounds shall be sent to the KC personnel department to resolve the cessation in service and for removal from the KC records." Similarly in the previous item, we see in the formulation of the procedure that the term KC Main Staff is being used?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question is: These are the notions and the terms that -- and regulations that refer to the status-related issues such as transfer and other things, and these are regulated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are regulated by the Law on the Army and other by-laws which serve for the implementation of the main law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was it necessary for any category of the service related status envisaged by the law to be regulated by this kind of order, if it pertains to the members of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now move to the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we have on our screens Exhibit P191, pages 1, both in the English and the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I was reading when both Mr. Starcevic and I mentioned KC, I think that everybody, the Chamber and everyone else know that this refers to the Personnel Centre, the acronym of which would be PC.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, this is the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska, Article 2 is something that I'm interested in and it reads as follows: "The military service in the army shall include military and other duties in the active duty and reserve forces in peacetime and wartime." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's a quotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this is a definition of the service which is more or less identical in all the relevant roles, including the Law on the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG STARCEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And in other countries as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Article 4 speaks about the relations in -- in the army, and this was the subject of our discussion at the beginning of this questioning and that is the relationship between the subordinates and superiors within the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now look at Article 153, page 15 in B/C/S, and page 22 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since you already commented this article, and it refers to the chain of command, can we look at page 36 in B/C/S and page 54 in English. Article 370, 36 in B/C/S, 54 in English. Article 370. This is a still the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska. If we can just scroll up in order for us to see which chapter we are dealing with in B/C/S. We're going to finish very soon for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's okay. [Interpretation] I would suggest that we adjourn for today, because we are entering now in a different area, and this is a very difficult chapter, and probably to give time, Mr. Starcevic, to rest. So we can adjourn two minutes before the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much, Mr. Lukic. We will take a break, Mr. Starcevic. I don't need to repeat myself. You know you don't have to talk to anybody. We come back tomorrow. Again, times have changed. We're still at 9.00 in the morning tomorrow, Courtroom I. Court adjourned.
